svg.text: Front-end evolution – the movement of "who makes the HTML, and when"
Each stage solved the previous stage's problem and created a new one in exchange
generated on the server
generated in the browser

g.text: ① Server templates
Sends complete HTML per request.
One click = a full page reload
+ simple · SEO friendly · fast first paint
- no partial updates · no app-like feel
② Ajax partial updates
Receives only data and edits part of the DOM.
imperative DOM handling of the jQuery era
+ interaction without reloading
- state scattered in the DOM, untrackable
③ SPA
The server gives an empty shell + JSON.
state → UI described declaratively
+ state in one place · complex UI possible
- whole bundle first · SEO · routing
④ Return to SSR · server components
Draw on the server first, sending only
the interactive pieces to the client
+ first paint recovered · less JS sent
- the server/client boundary enters the code

svg.text: The cost created when SSR came back – hydration
HTML made by the server only shows; it is not yet clickable. The browser has to build the same component tree again and attach events.

g.text: 1st – rendered on the server
HTML string generated → sent
the user sees the screen
2nd – rendered again in the browser
the same tree is rebuilt and matched to the DOM
during this time it shows but does not click
Answer – shrink the range redrawn
streaming · partial hydration · islands
only interactive pieces go to the client

svg.text: That "when it is visible" and "when it is usable" split apart is the core of this structure. Looking at a single metric hides the gap.
Server components approach this as "do not send it to the client at all". In exchange the developer must keep track of which code runs where.
When the place of rendering moves, the trust boundary moves with it
The illusion when moving to the client
When form validation, hiding menus by permission and
price calculation run in the browser, that is UI, not validation.
The attacker calls the API directly, without the screen.
The illusion when coming back to the server
A value in a server component feels server-only, and the moment
it is passed to a client component it is serialized and sent.
A new class of API keys and internal IDs leaking by this path appeared.
What does not change whatever the framework – all code and data running in the browser can be read and edited by the user.
XSS only changed address; it did not disappear. Frameworks escape strings by default, and ship an API that turns that off explicitly.
dangerouslySetInnerHTML · v-html · the bypassSecurityTrust family – this is why the warning is in the name.
That prototype pollution became a real attack path as code merging and copying client state objects multiplied is another change of this period.
